correctness.rationale: The graph is built exactly over GF(25). All 515 nonempty simplices are enumerated, all 75 elementary free-face pairs verified against remaining cofaces, and the spanning-tree presentation has 126 generators all eliminated by sound noncommutative Tietze substitutions. Euler characteristic 65 and the simply connected 2D CW Whitehead argument give wedge64 S2. All 25 translation actions are checked on oriented simplices: traces are 64 once, 4 twelve times, -1 twelve times. Strongly-regular neighbor counts (25,12,5,6) and Fourier inversion yield additive-character multiplicities 4,3,2, summing to 64. The verifier was executed from the scientific package and returned VERIFY_OK. This proves only the finite specified graph and its translation subgroup.

originality.rationale: The exact ordinary second Betti number is conclusively covered by Cioaba--Mim 2026 and is explicitly excluded from novelty. The accepted main theorem adds (i) a reproducible nonabelian finite Tietze certificate for simple connectivity and an integral wedge homotopy classification and, decisively, (ii) the full additive-translation character (64,4,-1) with character multiplicities 4/3/2. The published homology formula and general clique counts determine only homology dimensions and do not imply these equivariant multiplicities. Targeted published-finding corpus, own-ledger and primary-literature comparisons identified no stronger coverage of the complete theorem; this remains a best-evidence, not uniqueness, assessment.
residual_risks: An unindexed or inaccessible equivalent P25 equivariant-homology computation may exist.
The cycle-surgery proof in Cioaba--Mim may adapt to fundamental-group triviality; that does not itself cover the additive-translation character.
The 1996 Paley clique paper full text was not inspected, although its published stated focus is maximal cliques.

value.rationale: The 25-vertex Paley graph is the first nontrivial square-order example with three square-direction affine foliations. Known homology concentration leaves perfect fundamental groups and equivariant module structure undetermined. A complete, integral wedge homotopy type backed by explicit nonabelian elimination, together with the nonuniform multiplicities of all 25 additive characters, resolves structural invariants of a natural highly symmetric test object not fixed by Betti numbers. It creates an exact benchmark for future equivariant flag-complex calculations. No general-family theorem is claimed.
